descriptionAdvanced.en: Huanuni is the largest state-owned underground mining operation in Bolivia, centered on the rich tin deposits of the Posokoni hill in the Oruro Department. Since its nationalization in 2006, it has been managed by the Mining Corporation of Bolivia (COMIBOL) and remains a critical pillar of the nation's economy. The mine is famous for its high-grade ore and the extraordinary resilience of its workforce, which consists of thousands of traditional miners who often work in challenging conditions deep underground. Historically, Huanuni has been a bastion of the labor movement, with its union playing a decisive role in many of Bolivia's major political transformations. The city that has grown around the mine is a testament to a century of industrial labor and the deep cultural identity of the Andean mining community.

en: The Posokoni hill has been described as a 'mountain of tin' due to its incredible mineral density.
Huanuni produces approximately 1,000 metric tons of fine tin per month.
The mine operates at several levels, reaching depths of over 400 meters below the mountain's summit.
A massive new processing plant (Lucianita) was built recently to increase the mine's output and efficiency.
